To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interannual variability in cotton yields can be predicted using the GCM simulation of the regional atmospheric circulation and surface temperature fields.

(1) the interannual variability in cotton yields in the southeastern United states is significantly related to atmospheric circulation and temperature patterns in the spring and summer; (2) these atmospheric patterns can be predicted up to a month before the start of the growing season; and (3) predictions of these atmospheric circulation and surface temperature patterns from a global circulation models can be used to predict cotton yields in the Southeast up to 1 month before planting.
